target_platform.note: One measured target. Nothing here implies cross-platform support.

evidence_labeling.gui_driver: Playwright Electron API against the packaged application
evidence_labeling.process_cleanup: only exact process trees launched by the acceptance harness

product_claim: A root-scoped Windows workspace file manager lets a user select one real directory, inspect and navigate its contents, refresh external changes, select one or more entries, create a directory, rename, copy, move and send files or directories to the Windows Recycle Bin. It does not claim to replace Explorer.

primary_workflow.action: choose the pinned acceptance root and render its first exact directory snapshot
navigate into the pinned child directory and back to the selected root
perform an external create and remove, then refresh and render the new exact snapshot
select one entry, then select multiple entries by snapshot-scoped opaque entry IDs
create one directory with a single-segment name
rename one regular file without silent overwrite
copy one binary file and one directory tree within the selected root
move one regular file and one directory tree within the selected root
run one multi-entry mutation in which at least one entry succeeds and one controlled entry fails, and render partial per-entry outcomes
send one disposable file and one disposable directory tree to the Windows Recycle Bin without exposing permanent delete
close and relaunch the application, explicitly select the same root again, and render a fresh snapshot
an independent tree-and-byte oracle verifies every expected path, absence, payload and directory boundary

capability_acceptance_rule: Every active capability owns at least one positive and one independently failable attack row. Every row declares closed structured expected outcomes that its oracle must name with axis-qualified operation_status, snapshot_state and view_state markers. Mutation and selection rows separate operation status from snapshot state; directory-view rows leave operation status empty and separately declare complete or partial view state. Attack polarity must be carried by an adverse operation, snapshot or view outcome. Oracle and failure signal must remain distinct. Single and multiple selection, and file and directory-tree operations, remain distinct rows without inflating the capability count. No acceptance ID may be shared by two capabilities.

FM-ROOT-SELECT.action: select the pinned real directory through the GUI root picker
FM-ROOT-SELECT.oracle: [operation_status=accepted; snapshot_state=current] result is accepted; main returns the selected root identity and the exact current first snapshot; UI displays the root
FM-ROOT-SELECT.failure_signal: wrong root, missing snapshot, hidden root identity or renderer-supplied absolute path

FM-ROOT-CANCEL.action: cancel the GUI root picker without choosing a directory
FM-ROOT-CANCEL.oracle: [operation_status=cancelled; snapshot_state=unchanged] result is cancelled rather than refused; previous root and snapshot remain unchanged
FM-ROOT-CANCEL.failure_signal: cancellation becomes refusal/success, clears the current root or advances the snapshot

FM-ROOT-FAIL.action: run dynamic subject root-open-failure after a prior root is current: choose a separately proven ordinary non-reparse directory whose admitted initial snapshot read alone is fault-injected
FM-ROOT-FAIL.oracle: [operation_status=failed; snapshot_state=unchanged] result is typed failed; the prior root, snapshot and generation remain unchanged; no snapshot for the new root is fabricated; after cleanup the same new root passes a normal accepted control
FM-ROOT-FAIL.failure_signal: failure collapses into refused/cancelled, the new root replaces the prior root, generation advances, a fabricated snapshot appears, precondition is unproven, or the normal control fails

FM-ROOT-REFUSE.action: make the picker adapter return a regular file path and a missing directory path
FM-ROOT-REFUSE.oracle: [operation_status=refused; snapshot_state=unchanged] each structurally invalid selection is refused and the previous root and snapshot remain unchanged
FM-ROOT-REFUSE.failure_signal: a file or missing directory becomes the active root, cancellation is conflated with refusal, or the snapshot advances

FM-ROOT-REPARSE.action: offer a selected root that is itself a reparse point
FM-ROOT-REPARSE.oracle: [operation_status=refused; snapshot_state=unchanged] the root is refused by typed code and the previous snapshot remains unchanged
FM-ROOT-REPARSE.failure_signal: the product traverses the reparse root or reports generic success

FM-VIEW-MANIFEST.action: render the pinned root and child snapshots
FM-VIEW-MANIFEST.oracle: [snapshot_state=current; view_state=complete] view state is complete in the current snapshot; independent manifest comparison covers names, kinds and regular-file byte lengths
FM-VIEW-MANIFEST.failure_signal: missing, invented or mis-typed entry, or file size derived from renderer text

FM-VIEW-PARTIAL.action: make one controlled entry unreadable after proving the fixture precondition
FM-VIEW-PARTIAL.oracle: [snapshot_state=current; view_state=partial] view completeness is partial in the current snapshot with a typed observation error and is never rendered as an empty complete directory
FM-VIEW-PARTIAL.failure_signal: false empty, complete=true, silent omission or an attack that did not establish unreadability

FM-NAV-CHILD.action: navigate from the selected root into nav
FM-NAV-CHILD.oracle: [operation_status=accepted; snapshot_state=current] result is accepted and a new exact nav snapshot becomes current
FM-NAV-CHILD.failure_signal: wrong directory, reused generation or path supplied by renderer

FM-NAV-PARENT.action: navigate from nav back to the selected root
FM-NAV-PARENT.oracle: [operation_status=accepted; snapshot_state=current] result is accepted; a new exact root snapshot becomes current and navigation stops at that root
FM-NAV-PARENT.failure_signal: wrong parent, no new snapshot or navigation above root

FM-NAV-ESCAPE.action: first submit malformed IPC values (`..`, absolute path, ADS, reserved name and NUL) where an opaque entry_id is required; separately submit the real snapshot-scoped entry_id of dynamic subject escape-junction
FM-NAV-ESCAPE.oracle: [operation_status=refused; snapshot_state=unchanged] malformed payloads fail request-schema validation without path resolution; the well-formed junction entry_id reaches reparse policy and is refused before traversal; both return distinct typed codes and the snapshot remains unchanged
FM-NAV-ESCAPE.failure_signal: malformed text reaches path resolution, the junction is followed, both subcases collapse to one untyped error, or a new snapshot is published

FM-REFRESH-EXTERNAL.action: create and remove pinned entries outside the app, then invoke one GUI refresh
FM-REFRESH-EXTERNAL.oracle: [operation_status=accepted; snapshot_state=current] refresh is accepted; one new current snapshot is published and exactly reflects both external changes
FM-REFRESH-EXTERNAL.failure_signal: stale tree, more than one generation increment or fake live-sync before refresh

FM-REFRESH-STALE.action: retain a pre-refresh entry ID, replace the same-name file externally, refresh, then submit the old ID
FM-REFRESH-STALE.oracle: [operation_status=refused; snapshot_state=unchanged] the old ID is refused, the current replacement entry is untouched and its snapshot remains unchanged
FM-REFRESH-STALE.failure_signal: same-name substitution or an old ID mutates the new entry

FM-SELECT-SINGLE.action: select exactly one current entry ID
FM-SELECT-SINGLE.oracle: [operation_status=accepted; snapshot_state=current] selection is accepted; UI and main agree on that one ID and current generation
FM-SELECT-SINGLE.failure_signal: name-only selection, extra selected entry or generation mismatch

FM-SELECT-MULTI.action: select multiple distinct current entry IDs
FM-SELECT-MULTI.oracle: [operation_status=accepted; snapshot_state=current] selection is accepted; UI and main agree on exact current set membership, while selection order is not a product claim
FM-SELECT-MULTI.failure_signal: single-selection fallback, dropped member or silent duplicate collapse

FM-SELECT-STALE.action: submit missing, duplicate, unknown and cross-generation entry IDs
FM-SELECT-STALE.oracle: [operation_status=refused; snapshot_state=unchanged] the whole request is refused before mutation, the snapshot remains unchanged and every requested ID receives a typed refusal outcome
FM-SELECT-STALE.failure_signal: partial preflight mutation, deduplication or same-name substitution

FM-CREATE-DIRECTORY.action: create created-folder beneath the current directory
FM-CREATE-DIRECTORY.oracle: [operation_status=accepted; snapshot_state=current] result is accepted; one directory appears and one new snapshot becomes current
FM-CREATE-DIRECTORY.failure_signal: wrong kind, wrong parent, duplicate creation or missing snapshot

FM-CREATE-REFUSE.action: try empty, duplicate, reserved, ADS, separator and NUL-containing names
FM-CREATE-REFUSE.oracle: [operation_status=refused; snapshot_state=unchanged] each is refused, creates nothing and leaves the snapshot unchanged
FM-CREATE-REFUSE.failure_signal: normalization into a different name, partial creation or generation advance

FM-RENAME.action: rename rename-me.txt to renamed.txt using its current entry ID
FM-RENAME.oracle: [operation_status=accepted; snapshot_state=current] result is accepted; payload hash is unchanged, old path absent, new path present and one new snapshot becomes current
FM-RENAME.failure_signal: payload change, duplicate paths, wrong entry or wrong generation

FM-RENAME-CONFLICT.action: rename root entry rename-me.txt to the single-segment name rename-conflict.txt, which already exists with a different pinned payload; separately submit a stale source ID
FM-RENAME-CONFLICT.oracle: [operation_status=refused; snapshot_state=unchanged] both requests are refused; rename-me.txt and rename-conflict.txt retain their exact pre-operation bytes and the snapshot remains unchanged
FM-RENAME-CONFLICT.failure_signal: invalid-name refusal substitutes for conflict checking, either payload changes, source disappears, auto-rename occurs, stale source substitutes by name or generation advances

FM-COPY-FILE.action: copy copy-file.bin into dest-copy with one GUI batch command
FM-COPY-FILE.oracle: [operation_status=accepted; snapshot_state=current] result is accepted; source and destination payloads are byte-identical and one new snapshot becomes current
FM-COPY-FILE.failure_signal: text re-encoding, source removal, extra mutation or test-side copying

FM-COPY-DIRECTORY.action: copy the entire copy-dir tree into dest-copy with one GUI batch command
FM-COPY-DIRECTORY.oracle: [operation_status=accepted; snapshot_state=current] result is accepted; independent tree-and-byte oracle matches the current snapshot's every nested file and empty directory
FM-COPY-DIRECTORY.failure_signal: flattened tree, omitted empty directory, per-entry test loop or payload drift

FM-COPY-PARTIAL.action: copy one valid and one controlled unreadable member in one multi-entry request
FM-COPY-PARTIAL.oracle: [operation_status=partial; snapshot_state=current] overall status is partial, the resulting snapshot is current, every requested ID has an outcome, the valid copy is exact and the failed destination is absent
FM-COPY-PARTIAL.failure_signal: whole-batch success, whole-batch fiction, missing member outcome or silent partial data

FM-COPY-CONFLICT.action: copy copy-file.bin into dest-copy-conflict where dest-copy-conflict/copy-file.bin already exists with a different pinned payload
FM-COPY-CONFLICT.oracle: [operation_status=refused; snapshot_state=unchanged] request is refused; both source and sentinel retain exact pre-operation hashes and the snapshot is unchanged
FM-COPY-CONFLICT.failure_signal: silent overwrite, identical-byte laundering, auto-rename or generation advance

FM-MOVE-FILE.action: move move-file.txt into dest-move with one GUI batch command
FM-MOVE-FILE.oracle: [operation_status=accepted; snapshot_state=current] result is accepted; destination hash matches, source is absent and one new snapshot becomes current
FM-MOVE-FILE.failure_signal: copy-with-source-left, payload drift or more than one published snapshot

FM-MOVE-DIRECTORY.action: move the entire move-dir tree into dest-move with one GUI batch command
FM-MOVE-DIRECTORY.oracle: [operation_status=accepted; snapshot_state=current] result is accepted; the current destination tree is exact, the original tree is absent and empty/nested structure is preserved
FM-MOVE-DIRECTORY.failure_signal: partial unreported move, flattened tree or test-side per-entry move loop

FM-MOVE-PARTIAL.action: move one valid and one controlled locked member in one request
FM-MOVE-PARTIAL.oracle: [operation_status=partial; snapshot_state=current] overall status is partial, the resulting snapshot is current, successful source is absent, failed source remains, and every requested ID has an outcome
FM-MOVE-PARTIAL.failure_signal: all-success fiction, rollback fiction, missing member or wrong payload

FM-MOVE-CONFLICT.action: move move-file.txt into dest-move-conflict where dest-move-conflict/move-file.txt already exists with a different pinned payload; separately submit a stale destination-directory entry ID
FM-MOVE-CONFLICT.oracle: [operation_status=refused; snapshot_state=unchanged] both requests are refused; source and sentinel retain exact pre-operation hashes and the snapshot remains unchanged
FM-MOVE-CONFLICT.failure_signal: silent overwrite, source removal, identical-byte laundering, auto-rename, stale-ID substitution or generation advance

FM-TRASH-FILE.action: send trash-file.txt through the native Windows recycle operation
FM-TRASH-FILE.oracle: [operation_status=accepted; snapshot_state=current] result is accepted; source leaves the current root snapshot and independent native evidence identifies a recoverable recycle operation
FM-TRASH-FILE.failure_signal: permanent deletion, source disappearance alone or stubbed evidence reported as native

FM-TRASH-DIRECTORY.action: send the disposable trash-dir tree through the native Windows recycle operation
FM-TRASH-DIRECTORY.oracle: [operation_status=accepted; snapshot_state=current] result is accepted; whole tree leaves the current root snapshot and native recoverability evidence is recorded
FM-TRASH-DIRECTORY.failure_signal: permanent recursive delete, partial silent deletion or file-only implementation

FM-TRASH-REFUSE.action: submit stale, out-of-root and reparse entry IDs and force one controlled native failure
FM-TRASH-REFUSE.oracle: [operation_status=refused; operation_status=failed; snapshot_state=unchanged] every refused or failed outcome is typed; zero-mutation results leave the snapshot unchanged; no permanent-delete fallback exists
FM-TRASH-REFUSE.failure_signal: target disappears, fallback deletion, wrong status or fabricated recovery evidence

FM-SYS-RESULT-UNION.action: drive FM-COPY-FILE, FM-COPY-PARTIAL and FM-COPY-CONFLICT, then run dynamic subject locked-member as a single-entry move so no member succeeds
FM-SYS-RESULT-UNION.oracle: the four results are respectively accepted, partial, refused and failed; every requested entry ID has exactly one typed outcome
FM-SYS-RESULT-UNION.failure_signal: any two overall statuses collapse, refusal is reported for admitted I/O failure, or a requested ID has no outcome

FM-SYS-SNAPSHOT-SEQUENCE.action: publish the initial root snapshot, run dynamic subject unchanged-refresh, run FM-REFRESH-EXTERNAL, then run FM-COPY-FILE
FM-SYS-SNAPSHOT-SEQUENCE.oracle: each completed observation publishes exactly one next generation, including the byte-identical refresh; per-entry status, not generation, says whether mutation occurred
FM-SYS-SNAPSHOT-SEQUENCE.failure_signal: generation skips/reuses, unchanged refresh publishes nothing, one operation publishes multiple generations, or client infers mutation from generation

FM-SYS-SNAPSHOT-UNAVAILABLE.action: run dynamic subject post-operation-snapshot-failure: perform one real GUI copy of partial/ok.bin to dest-copy/post-scan.bin, then make only the immediately following main-process scan return snapshot_read_failed
FM-SYS-SNAPSHOT-UNAVAILABLE.oracle: the entry outcome and overall status report the successful copy, snapshot.state is unavailable, last_published_generation is unchanged and a typed snapshot_read_failed code is present; the external oracle sees exact destination bytes
FM-SYS-SNAPSHOT-UNAVAILABLE.failure_signal: current/unchanged snapshot is fabricated, mutation is hidden, destination bytes are wrong, generation advances without a published snapshot, or the failure is untyped

FM-SYS-ENTRY-ID-SCOPE.action: after FM-REFRESH-EXTERNAL publishes a new snapshot, resubmit pre-refresh IDs through FM-REFRESH-STALE and FM-SELECT-STALE
FM-SYS-ENTRY-ID-SCOPE.oracle: every old ID is refused before mutation and same-name entries in the new snapshot remain untouched
FM-SYS-ENTRY-ID-SCOPE.failure_signal: an old ID revives, name equality substitutes identity, or any mutation occurs

FM-SYS-PATH-AUTHORITY.action: run FM-NAV-ESCAPE and FM-CREATE-REFUSE while recording the renderer/preload request payloads
FM-SYS-PATH-AUTHORITY.oracle: renderer payloads contain only snapshot generation, opaque entry IDs and validated single-segment names; no path or filesystem handle crosses the boundary
FM-SYS-PATH-AUTHORITY.failure_signal: absolute/relative path or handle reaches renderer, malformed entry_id reaches path resolution, or renderer performs containment

FM-SYS-REPARSE.action: list escape-junction, then run FM-ROOT-REPARSE, the junction arm of FM-NAV-ESCAPE and the reparse arm of FM-TRASH-REFUSE
FM-SYS-REPARSE.oracle: the entry is visibly typed reparse, while selected reparse root, traversal and mutation are refused with typed codes and unchanged snapshot
FM-SYS-REPARSE.failure_signal: junction is hidden as ordinary directory, followed, mutated, or admitted by resolved-string containment

FM-SYS-NO-OVERWRITE.action: run FM-RENAME-CONFLICT, FM-COPY-CONFLICT and FM-MOVE-CONFLICT against their different-byte pinned sentinels
FM-SYS-NO-OVERWRITE.oracle: every source and sentinel retains its exact pre-operation hash; no auto-rename occurs and the snapshot is unchanged
FM-SYS-NO-OVERWRITE.failure_signal: any sentinel/source changes, disappears or is renamed, even if the final bytes happen to match

FM-SYS-ACTION-SHAPE.action: time FM-COPY-DIRECTORY and FM-MOVE-DIRECTORY from one GUI command each over the exact pinned subtrees
FM-SYS-ACTION-SHAPE.oracle: instrument records one renderer dispatch and one final result/snapshot per operation; the external oracle validates the whole resulting tree
FM-SYS-ACTION-SHAPE.failure_signal: test-side per-entry loop, internal service injection, different fixture, pre-copy/pre-move or cap attached to another action

FM-SYS-NO-PERMANENT-DELETE.action: enumerate renderer/preload/main command surfaces, then run both native trash positives and trash-failure
FM-SYS-NO-PERMANENT-DELETE.oracle: only recoverable native recycle operation exists; no permanent-delete command or fallback is reachable
FM-SYS-NO-PERMANENT-DELETE.failure_signal: permanent delete surface exists, fallback executes, or source disappearance alone is called recoverability

FM-SYS-RELAUNCH-RESELECT.action: run dynamic subject relaunch-reselect: close packaged PID A gracefully, prove it exited, launch packaged PID B where B differs from A, explicitly select the same pinned root through the labeled picker path and wait for its first snapshot
FM-SYS-RELAUNCH-RESELECT.oracle: PID B is new, no root appears before explicit selection, and the selected root publishes a fresh initial snapshot without remembered-root claim
FM-SYS-RELAUNCH-RESELECT.failure_signal: same process is reused, remembered root is silently restored, selection is bypassed, or no fresh snapshot is published

root_selection_meanings.accepted: an existing non-reparse directory becomes the selected root and publishes its first snapshot
root_selection_meanings.cancelled: the picker returns no selection and the previous root/snapshot remain unchanged
root_selection_meanings.refused: a returned subject is not an existing non-reparse directory and the previous root/snapshot remain unchanged
root_selection_meanings.failed: the picker or admitted root-open operation fails operationally without replacing the previous root

per_entry_meanings.refused: policy or a precondition rejected this entry before its mutation
per_entry_meanings.failed: this entry was admitted to execution and its I/O failed

operation_result.partial: at least one requested entry succeeded and at least one was refused or failed
operation_result.refused: no requested entry succeeded, no entry reached execution failure, and policy or preconditions refused the request or every member before mutation
operation_result.failed: no requested entry succeeded and at least one admitted entry reached execution failure; other entries may have been refused

snapshot.current: contains the newly published snapshot after observation succeeds
snapshot.unchanged: contains the exact prior snapshot when no mutation occurred and no new snapshot was published
snapshot.unavailable: contains no fabricated snapshot; reports last_published_generation and a typed observation code

reparse.later_revision_requires: handle-based or equivalently evidenced confinement before any in-root reparse permission

deferred_capabilities.rationale: Electron and the Windows default-application route do not promise a new child PID and may reuse an existing process. A test helper would measure a different operation.
deferred_capabilities.revisit_gate: a bounded native acceptance can identify ownership and clean only processes it launched without changing the default-application operation

fixture_contract.root_location: fresh D-drive scratch directory created per run; never a user folder

dynamic_subjects.operation: list the junction, then submit its current entry_id to navigate and trash operations
dynamic_subjects.precondition: create root/escape-junction as a Windows junction to a sibling disposable directory named escape-target-${run_id} outside the selected root
dynamic_subjects.precondition_proof: lstat identifies a reparse point and an independent canonical-target query proves the target is outside the selected root before either attack
dynamic_subjects.expected: entry is visibly typed reparse; navigate and trash are refused with distinct typed codes; snapshot and outside target remain unchanged
dynamic_subjects.cleanup: remove only root/escape-junction, then remove sibling escape-target-${run_id}; verify the rest of the pinned root still matches its manifest

dynamic_subjects.operation: first move partial/locked.bin alone to prove overall failed; then move partial/ok.bin plus partial/locked.bin in one batch to prove partial
dynamic_subjects.precondition: a harness-owned helper opens partial/locked.bin with a Windows share mode that denies the exact move/delete operation
dynamic_subjects.precondition_proof: the helper reports its exact PID/handle and a direct control move fails with sharing violation before the product request
dynamic_subjects.expected: single-entry result is failed; multi-entry result is partial; locked source hash remains pinned, successful source/destination are exact, and every ID has an outcome
dynamic_subjects.cleanup: close only the recorded helper handle/process in finally, remove dest-move/locked.bin if present, and restore partial/ok.bin from pinned payload

dynamic_subjects.operation: render the parent view, then copy partial/ok.bin plus partial/unreadable.bin in one batch
dynamic_subjects.precondition: save the exact ACL of partial/unreadable.bin, deny the current test identity the read operation used by metadata/copy, and leave sibling partial/ok.bin readable
dynamic_subjects.precondition_proof: an independent read/stat control fails for partial/unreadable.bin and succeeds for partial/ok.bin before the product actions
dynamic_subjects.expected: view is partial rather than false-empty; copy result is partial; unreadable source hash is unchanged and dest-copy/unreadable.bin is absent
dynamic_subjects.cleanup: restore the saved ACL exactly in finally, remove dest-copy/unreadable.bin if present, and verify both pinned source hashes

dynamic_subjects.operation: outside the app remove refresh/base.txt and create refresh/external-added.bin with payload hex a1b2c3d4, then invoke one GUI refresh
dynamic_subjects.precondition: refresh/base.txt has its pinned hash and refresh/external-added.bin is absent in the current snapshot
dynamic_subjects.precondition_proof: independent tree-and-byte oracle records the precondition immediately before the external write/remove
dynamic_subjects.expected: one new snapshot omits base.txt, includes external-added.bin with 4 bytes and SHA-256 97ed8e55519b020c4d9aceb40e0d3bc7eaa22d080d49592bf21206cb697c8a58, and invalidates every old entry_id
dynamic_subjects.cleanup: remove external-added.bin, restore base.txt from pinned payload, invoke no product operation during cleanup, and re-run the independent oracle

dynamic_subjects.operation: submit the current entry_id of partial/trash-locked.txt to the native recycle operation
dynamic_subjects.precondition: a harness-owned helper opens the exact file with delete sharing denied
dynamic_subjects.precondition_proof: the helper reports exact PID/handle and a control native recycle attempt fails before the product request
dynamic_subjects.expected: overall and per-entry status are failed, the source retains its pinned hash, snapshot is unchanged and no permanent-delete fallback is invoked
dynamic_subjects.cleanup: close only the recorded helper handle/process in finally and verify partial/trash-locked.txt remains byte-exact

dynamic_subjects.operation: from the packaged GUI issue one copy of partial/ok.bin to dest-copy/post-scan.bin while the acceptance-owned main-process filesystem adapter delegates the real copy and fails only the immediately following snapshot scan with code snapshot_read_failed
dynamic_subjects.precondition: adapter is inactive for launch and initial snapshot, target is absent, and source has its pinned hash
dynamic_subjects.precondition_proof: adapter event log proves exactly one armed post-mutation scan failure and the external oracle proves the destination did not exist before dispatch
dynamic_subjects.expected: copy entry is accepted, overall status is accepted, snapshot state is unavailable with snapshot_read_failed and last published generation, and destination bytes equal partial/ok.bin
dynamic_subjects.cleanup: disarm the adapter in finally, remove dest-copy/post-scan.bin, run a real refresh and require a current snapshot before the next case

dynamic_subjects.operation: invoke one GUI refresh without changing any fixture path or byte
dynamic_subjects.precondition: independent oracle captures the exact current manifest and generation
dynamic_subjects.precondition_proof: oracle rechecks the same manifest immediately before refresh dispatch
dynamic_subjects.expected: one byte-identical new snapshot is published at previous generation plus one and no per-entry mutation is reported
dynamic_subjects.cleanup: no filesystem cleanup; re-run oracle and prove the fixture manifest stayed identical

dynamic_subjects.operation: with the pinned root A already current, use the labeled picker path to select a sibling ordinary directory root-B-${run_id}; the acceptance-owned main-process adapter admits B and fails only B's first snapshot read with typed code root_snapshot_read_failed
dynamic_subjects.precondition: root A has a current snapshot; root-B-${run_id} exists, is an ordinary non-reparse directory and is independently enumerable; the adapter is inactive for A and armed for exactly one B initial-snapshot read
dynamic_subjects.precondition_proof: independent lstat/canonical/enumeration controls prove B is a valid ordinary root and the adapter log proves one pending B-only read failure before picker confirmation
dynamic_subjects.expected: root-selection result is failed with root_snapshot_read_failed; A remains selected with byte-identical snapshot and generation; no B snapshot is published or fabricated
dynamic_subjects.cleanup: disarm the adapter in finally, select B again through the same labeled picker and require an accepted normal snapshot, explicitly reselect A, then remove only root-B-${run_id}

dynamic_subjects.operation: gracefully close packaged PID A, launch packaged PID B, then explicitly select the same pinned root through the labeled picker path
dynamic_subjects.precondition: PID A and its process tree were launched by this harness and the root matches the independent manifest
dynamic_subjects.precondition_proof: wait for PID A to exit, record PID B and prove B differs from A before root selection
dynamic_subjects.expected: no root is active before explicit selection; selection publishes a fresh initial snapshot that matches the oracle and makes no remembered-root claim
dynamic_subjects.cleanup: gracefully close PID B, then terminate only B's exact process tree if graceful exit fails; never kill by image or command-line census

timing_policy.purpose: hang detection only; no fast, responsive or cross-machine latency verdict

product_hang.requires: the exact bounded action, subject and timer boundaries were proven and environment controls do not explain the breach

instrument_subject_mismatch.requires: evidence shows the harness performed an action or subject outside bounded_actions

environment_limit.requires: recorded environment evidence explains why the exact bounded action cannot be judged on this run

bounded_actions.subject: copy-dir exact manifest subtree
bounded_actions.timer_start: renderer dispatch of the user command
bounded_actions.timer_stop: overall result and snapshot state are rendered
bounded_actions.forbidden_substitution: test-side per-entry loop, pre-copy, internal service call or different fixture

bounded_actions.subject: move-dir exact manifest subtree
bounded_actions.timer_start: renderer dispatch of the user command
bounded_actions.timer_stop: overall result and snapshot state are rendered
bounded_actions.forbidden_substitution: test-side per-entry loop, pre-move, internal service call or different fixture

comparator.scope: one conventional main-process filesystem operation-core artifact; not a second GUI product
comparator.same_subject: same main-process operation subset, pinned fixture manifest, operation vectors and independent tree-and-byte oracle
comparator.topology: ordinary imperative handlers with no predeclared MSSP set decomposition
comparator.quantitative_claim_gate: implementation size, defect, blast-radius or verification-effort comparisons require the executable comparator and the same bounded protocol; otherwise each is NotMeasured

topology.what_is_preregistered: product, capability, cross-cutting contract, fixture, evidence and comparator boundaries only
topology.forbidden_default: do not copy App-1 module topology, document capabilities or encoding boundaries into App 2
topology.next_step: three architects derive and attest a separate App-2 MSSP core after this preregistration survives attack

membership.role_change: any reviewer who edits later product code becomes a builder for that exact commit and cannot supply the only independent acceptance

general: denominator deletion or reclassification after results
foundation stuffing and cheap-share expensive-adaptation laundering
author tests accepted as independent evidence
slice_specific: generation is misread as a mutation counter instead of snapshot identity
partial mutation plus unavailable post-operation scan is forced into a fabricated current or unchanged snapshot
policy refusal and admitted execution failure collapse into one status
old snapshot ID mutates a same-name replacement
reparse string containment is cited as race-safe authority
one batch result omits a requested entry or flattens partial failure
copy or move timing measures a test-side loop or different subject
file-only behavior is reported as directory support
source disappearance is reported as Recycle Bin recoverability
permanent delete is exposed as a fallback

stop_boundary: This artifact authorizes only preregistration review. No App-2 product record or production code begins until the exact preregistration is green under its own verifier and drills, Elenchos completes first independent attack, Pragma completes denominator/acceptance-row attack, and all three architects approve the exact digest. Product implementation additionally requires a separately agreed App-2 MSSP core, work package, pinned fixture materialization and acceptance ownership. No provider call, main merge, release, deployment, publication or MSSP method adoption is authorized here.
